The season began on March 5 and finished on December 3.{{cite web|url=http://www.j-league.or.jp/release/000/00003808.html |title=2011 J. League tournament details |publisher=J.League official website |language=ja |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101224083119/http://www.j-league.or.jp/release/000/00003808.html |archive-date=2010-12-24 }} Due to the aftermath of the [[2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami]], the season was put on hold from March 12 to April 23.{{cite web|title=J.League agrees to resume games on April 23 |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/soccer/03/22/jleague.resume/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104033721/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/soccer/03/22/jleague.resume/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 4, 2012|work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=27 March 2011}} [[FC Tokyo]] won the tournament and returned to [[J.League Division 1|J1]] immediately after being relegated the previous season. By virtue of winning the [[2011 Emperor's Cup]] final, they earned a berth in the [[2012 AFC Champions League]] as well. [[Sagan Tosu]] and [[Hokkaido Consadole Sapporo|Consadole Sapporo]] finished second and third, respectively, and also won the promotion. Consadole are returning to the top flight after three years of absence, while for Tosu this is the first promotion in their history. Sagan became the last of [[1999 J.League Division 2|original ten J2 teams]] to reach J1, passing the moniker of the longest-staying D2 dweller to [[Mito HollyHock]]. ==Teams== As in the previous seasons, the size of the league was increased by one team to twenty overall. [[Gainare Tottori]] as [[2010 Japan Football League]] champions were promoted. [[Kashiwa Reysol]] as champions of the [[2010 J.League Division 2|2010 season]], runners-up [[Ventforet Kofu]] and third-placed team [[Avispa Fukuoka]] were promoted to the [[2011 J.League Division 1]]. Kashiwa made their immediate return to the top division, while Kofu and Fukuoka ended three- and four-year tenures in the J2. The three teams were replaced by [[FC Tokyo]], [[Kyoto Sanga FC]] and [[Shonan Bellmare]], who were relegated at the end of the [[2010 J.League Division 1]] season after finishing in the bottom three places of the table. Shonan only made a cameo appearance at the D1, Kyoto re-entered the second level of the Japanese league pyramid after three years, and Tokyo eventually had to return to the J2 for the first time after eleven seasons. {{location map+ |Japan Greater Tokyo area|float=right |width=450 |caption=Locations of the 2011 J.League 2 teams |places= {{location map~ |Japan Greater Tokyo area|lat=43.015100 |long=141.409816 |label=
